\begin{abstract}

We conduct an event study of US bank stock (KBE) responses to Federal Reserve target-rate announcements from December 2015 through December 2025. Using a market model with the S\&P 500 (SPY) as benchmark, we estimate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for 31 FOMC announcements. Over the pre-registered event window $[-1, +1]$ (three trading days centered on the announcement), rate hikes ($n=20$) yield mean CAR of $-1.06\%$ <!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_hikes_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.estimate --> ($t = -1.998$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_hikes_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.t_stat -->, $p = 0.0603$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_hikes_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.p_value -->), not significant at the 5\% level; rate cuts ($n=11$) yield mean CAR of $-0.08\%$ <!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_cuts_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.estimate --> ($t = -0.091$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_cuts_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.t_stat -->, $p = 0.9295$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_cuts_m1p1.coefficients.mean_car.p_value -->), not significant. Testing surprise sensitivity via regression of CARs on the day-0 change in the 2-year Treasury yield (basis points), the pooled coefficient across all 31 events is $-0.0208$ bps <!-- src: estimation_results.json#H2.coefficients.beta.estimate --> ($p = 0.6368$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#H2.coefficients.beta.p_value -->), not significant. A secondary, non-pre-registered analysis of the window $[0, +5]$ shows pooled mean CAR of $-1.47\%$ <!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_pooled_0p5.coefficients.mean_car.estimate --> ($p = 0.022$<!-- src: estimation_results.json#h1_pooled_0p5.coefficients.mean_car.p_value -->), significant at the 5\% level. Bank stock responses to FOMC announcements are limited in the immediate announcement window, with cumulative losses appearing over the week following the announcement.

\end{abstract}
